alt: Blue cotton covered in rows of red, black and white circles, with a wide red border of scalloped medallions at the bottom.
caption: Pieces of an ajrakh shawl or cover made in Sind, about 1855–79 (V&A 5473A/(IS)): a blue field of large and small circles with an end border of floral medallions.

alt: Long white cotton printed with rows of small animals, trees, temples and riders in red, black and blue.
caption: Dress fabric, Machilipatnam, 1879, block printed with pen work. The museum says it was probably made for export to Iran; it bears a printed Persian inscription.

alt: End of a white cloth with rows of red and black sprigs, a band of large red flowers and a square black stamp.
caption: Wrapped garment, probably Sanganer, about 1855–79, with a black octroi (tax collection) stamp (V&A 4497(IS)). Dupattas printed at Sanganer carry dated octroi stamps.

alt: Several carved wooden printing blocks set out in a row along a stone ledge.
caption: Printing blocks, [Ajrakhpur], [Kutch].
credit: Rick Bradley, "printing blocks, ajrakpur, kaach", Flickr, CC BY 2.0

alt: Close view of a carved wooden printing block with a leaf-pattern border, resting among other blocks.
caption: Wooden blocks used for kalamkari printing in Machilipatnam.
credit: Courtesy J. Niranjan, Srikalahasti / Sahapedia, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

alt: A heap of used carved wooden printing blocks lying on the floor beneath a printing table.
caption: Used printing blocks under the printing table in a small cottage-industry factory. Sanganer, Rajasthan, India.
